--secondary; action='store_true'; help='Also vary page-cache size, temporary lifetimes and raw reads'

entries.purpose: `make -C tests run-swift-storage` runs the standalone Swift package's Core and local SQLCipher Runtime tests without building NV. First run `bash tools/build-storage-deps.sh` from the repository root; SwiftPM resolves the pinned Swift Crypto dependency. `SWIFT_STORAGE_TEST_FLAGS` selects an optimized/sanitized build. `make -C tests run-swift-storage-phase2` additionally verifies fresh-process recovery, independent envelopes/fixtures, schema equality, C diagnostics and ordinary/same-module compiler boundaries. It includes the [Phase 3 connected checks](impl-proposal-5/plan/phase3-validation.md): independent stores exchanging real bytes, editable multi-head Current, exact source-entry exclusion, conflict-copy dispositions, actual compensation inverses and failure/restart schedules. Set `SWIFT_STORAGE_PHASE2_FLAGS='--configuration release --mutations'` for the optimized isolated challenge campaigns. The [Phase 2 report](impl-proposal-5/plan/phase2-local-runtime-validation.md) records underlying acceptance/fault coverage. These use synthetic private stores, not real user collections or providers. The test runner's availability is separate from the library's declared macOS 11.5 deployment target.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/IntegrationTests.md#Root-lock interference probe / Cold startup with an evicted lock
entries.name: Root-lock interference probe / Cold startup with an evicted lock
entries.purpose: Cold startup with an evicted lock — Run `root-lock-evict ROOT RUN cold`, then `NV_ICLOUD_API_TEST_TIMEOUT=10 ... root-lock-watch ROOT RUN cold`. Require actual `not-downloaded-observed=1`; inspect `before-open dataless`, open latency, and local contention. Open may succeed while the empty file remains dataless. Request acceptance alone does not exercise eviction.
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Root-lock interference probe / Eviction/rematerialization while held
entries.purpose: Eviction/rematerialization while held — Start `root-lock-watch ROOT RUN held` for 60 seconds. After its holder-acquired line, use another process on that same Mac for `root-lock-evict ROOT RUN held`, then `root-lock-download ROOT RUN held`. Record refusal separately. If refused, the transition was not exercised; do not call it a successful eviction test. Repeat by evicting `cold` **before** opening, holding that dataless lock, and requesting `root-lock-download ROOT RUN cold` while held.
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/IntegrationTests.md#Root-lock interference probe / Remote replacement while held
entries.name: Root-lock interference probe / Remote replacement while held
entries.purpose: Remote replacement while held — On Mac A, start `root-lock-watch ROOT RUN held` for 60 seconds. After acquisition, run `root-lock-replace ROOT RUN held` on Mac B. This explicitly installs another **empty** file with coordinated Foundation replacement. A local install on B does not prove delivery to A: require A's name/descriptor identity change before claiming replacement was exercised. Reverse roles in a fresh run.
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/IntegrationTests.md#Root-lock interference probe / Concurrent creation on two Macs
entries.name: Root-lock interference probe / Concurrent creation on two Macs
entries.purpose: Concurrent creation on two Macs — On both Macs run `root-lock-watch ROOT RUN race START_EPOCH` using the same epoch 15–30 seconds ahead. Each process checks absence and then uses exclusive creation; both logs must show `exclusive-created=1` and overlapping held intervals. An `EEXIST` result is inconclusive, not concurrent creation. Neither process changes the empty lock afterward. Watch for provider-created replacement, extra siblings/unresolved versions, and second-local-process admission. Use a fresh session for every round.
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/IntegrationTests.md#Section: Repeat on each Mac, against its existing iCloud API test directory:
entries.name: Section: Repeat on each Mac, against its existing iCloud API test directory:
entries.purpose: NV_ICLOUD_API_TEST_TIMEOUT=30 /tmp/notation-integration-tests/ICloudAPIContractTest \   root-lock-directory "$ICLOUD_API_TEST_ROOT" ``` Independent exec'ed processes verify exclusion initially, after closing a separately opened catalog descriptor, after coordinated child-file creation/Foundation replacement, after directory rename and movement to another parent, and across a duplicated-descriptor handoff. Closing the last descriptor permits acquisition. A pipe-confirmed independent holder is killed with `SIGKILL`, after which another process must acquire. Recreating the old pathname deliberately produces a **different**, independently lockable directory: this positive control must not be interpreted as protection of a pathname or a replacement root. On a positively ubiquitous directory with an uploaded child, the probe also requests directory eviction, opens/locks it again, materializes the exact child bytes while locked, and repeats eviction/rematerialization while holding the lock. It records directory `SF_DATALESS` separately from the child's not-downloaded status. **Child-only eviction does not establish directory-placeholder coverage.** That case still exercises child rematerialization and exclusion, but returns 2 to retain the stronger coverage gap. Eviction acceptance alone, refusal, and missing upload evidence are not successful lifecycle observations. The shared process/contender deadlines above apply, and synthetic subtrees are retained.

entries.name: Section: 6. Tests and next implementation gate
entries.purpose: Current command: `make -C tests run-swift-storage` (native Swift Testing; no app/simulator; initial dependency resolution downloads the pinned packages). Literal scalar and complete-note fixtures cover exact composed/decomposed spelling, case-distinct labels, NUL/CRLF, malformed UTF-8, every truncation point, trailing bytes, attacker-sized prefixes, finite date precision and invalid/noncanonical dates. Operation fixtures independently specify canonical preimages, hashes and transport bytes for all six implemented kinds. They check semantic-field changes, local/external/table remapping, stale local-reference contexts, preserved unresolved external claims, and record sizes below/at/above the 64-MiB ceiling. These tests use ordinary public import, not `@testable`; they do not qualify whole-action admission or an OS persistence primitive. After building the package, run `python3 tools/test-swift-storage-types.py --modules <build-bin-path>/Modules` from the repository root. Obtain that bin path with `swift build --package-path NVStorage --show-bin-path` using the same scratch/configuration options as the build. The script checks an ordinary client first, then requires specific compiler rejections for action/segment-versus-operation identity, causal parents versus note predecessors, identity reassignment and a forged claimed-ID constructor. An unrelated import/compiler error does not count as a passing negative control. The ordinary local save/reopen slice is now implemented and tested in the [Phase 2 report](phase2-local-runtime-validation.md). Before expanding it to the complete storage engine:

entries.purpose: **WP0: Pin sources and qualify tooling.** Reuse the repository test/build/API-contract assets linked in §1. Record normative snapshots and active model dispositions. Implement the adopted package-runner/Makefile integration; confirm compiler/dependency/deployment settings. Resolve unfinished format choices only where needed for the first supported record slice. Inventory real mutation entrypoints and acceptance/private-state issuers. **Deliverable:** a short symbol-to-responsibility map, existing commands that actually run, source/fixture provenance, and an initial list of blocked items. **Exit:** an ordinary separate client and representative target executable build; no claim yet of storage conformance. **WP1: Add the minimum observations and fixtures.** Create a complete valid baseline collection with N and untouched U, required bootstrap/completion evidence, independent initial values, and named low-level effect gates. Implement the small disk-model examples and observer negative controls. Add TC-STATIC-01–04 for actual available APIs. **Exit:** the fixture's independent inspector and available hook/static-client self-tests pass; missing hooks/fake compiler failures/incorrect expected bytes fail the harness. Opening that baseline through the production codec/installer is a G1 exit, after WP2/WP3 implement the path. Unsupported records remain unavailable rather than assigned temporary production tags.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/impl-proposal-5/plan/swift-storage-conformance-testing-strategy.md#Section: G1 — Qualify a local saved-edit slice before expanding the abstraction
entries.name: Section: G1 — Qualify a local saved-edit slice before expanding the abstraction
entries.purpose: **WP2: Minimal value, action, byte and encrypted envelope path.** Freeze the necessary complete records and before/after references, not every deferred feature. Implement TC-CAP-01, TC-BYTE-01–02, TC-CRYPT-01, and applicable limits/zstd cases. Run actual selected primitive known-answer tests and bootstrap framing checks. Use both profiles before qualifying both. **WP3: Actual installer, pin commit, reopen and completion.** Implement TC-DUR-01–05, TC-EVD-01, TC-ASY-01's local variants and TC-LIVE-01. Exercise actual lower-level I/O and fresh-process recovery; run M01–05, M10–14 where applicable. Cover settings-versus-pin concurrency, not just object creation. **Exit:** complete acknowledged groups and required closure survive the specified reopen boundary; unacknowledged complete finals are rediscovered; no stale completion clears newer work; every critical challenge has a meaningful disposition. At least one actual OS run connects the installer to its selected primitive contract. Full physical power-loss qualification remains distinct at G4. **Scope control:** G1 is a development gate for the supported slice, not permission to ship proposal 5 without required history, repair, source-preserving legacy/unsupported-input handling or other enabled-feature gates. New rich codecs are deferred and attachments unsupported. A symbolic or public-only prototype does not qualify both profiles.

Use two independent store instances and a fresh-process variant, not shared in-memory indexes. Run M06–09, M14–15, M20 and relevant earlier challenges. Extend model connections only for the specific compositions. Use the [phase-3 matrix](phase3-schedule-observation-matrix.md#4-feature-matrix) for the portable semantic portion of WP4; retain startup/repair and application/ provider obligations in their respective later gates. entries.name: Section: 10. Limits that force implementation and test maintenance
entries.purpose: Create a closed `ProtocolLimit` registry whose entries record units, inclusive/exclusive boundaries, stage, and rejection/deferral policy. Preserve the existing object, descriptor, stamp, passphrase, and merge limits; do not invent values for the remaining TODO rows. [P3] Separate it from `WorkBudget`. Protocol limits define accepted representations; scheduling budgets govern how much work a machine does in one pass. Exhausting a traversal/fetch budget yields resumable deferred work, not invalid history or a truncated frontier. Ordinary collections must not age out because an arbitrary total ancestry-depth cap was added. Choose unfinished limits using realistic input rates, whole-note memory and NSTextView/synchronous-search measurements, with headroom for action metadata and before/after representations. Preserve the fixed wire ceilings unless explicitly reviewed; no speculative live-note paging or oversized-note subsystem. Small current notes do not bound retained-history growth. [P3]

entries.purpose: Compile intentionally invalid snippets against the ordinary built module: pass an `ActionID` as an `OperationID`; pass scope parents as a compensation target; attempt publication with parsed-only input; construct an acceptance receipt; decode a physical permission from storage; or consume a unique ticket twice. Each case must fail for the expected diagnostic category at the intended line, with a positive companion using the valid API. A missing module, unrelated syntax error, or linker failure is not successful enforcement evidence. Pin the compiler used for diagnostic matching and update expectations deliberately on toolchain changes. Source/API checks should also reject accidental escape hatches: public unchecked constructors, conformance of authority types to `Decodable`, unconstrained raw path publication, safety-disabling flags, and unreviewed unsafe annotations. Use narrowly scoped syntax-aware checks where needed; avoid claiming that a string grep is a proof of architectural isolation.

entries.name: Section: Golden bytes, generated inputs, and property tests
entries.purpose: Use the package's native Swift tests for parameterized fixtures, invoked through the existing Makefile on macOS and directly in portable jobs. Keep standalone legacy suites; qualify test-runner availability separately from the macOS 11.5 library/bridge executable. No third-party/duplicate test framework is needed. Keep synthetic fixture bytes, decoded values, exact canonical preimages, expected IDs, expected classifications, and provenance together. Encode large test integers as explicit decimal strings or byte encodings where JSON tooling could otherwise lose precision. Add deterministic generators for valid operations and DAGs, followed by targeted invalid mutations. Preserve seeds and minimize failures. Useful properties include equal complete histories reducing identically across delivery permutations; duplicate receipt being idempotent; transport repacking preserving operation identity; Current-only edits preserving unrelated alternatives; and restoration/compensation maintaining distinct births. Do not turn those into invalid global assertions: derived live notes are not monotonic because obsolete automatic preservation may retract, and an untouched copy’s eligibility can change as Deletes arrive. Accepted evidence is retained; the derived view can legitimately change. [P2]

entries.id: planned-check:docs/tla/Incarnation-Metadata-Experiments.md#Section: First finding: fix the test's attribute-name contract
entries.name: Section: First finding: fix the test's attribute-name contract
entries.purpose: The older runtime's `xattr_name_with_flags` omitted the unsupported `ONLY_SAVING` bit: the same source call generated `#SX` on 26 but `#S` on 14, `#PSX` versus `#PS`, and `#X` versus no suffix. The first peer inspection recomputed names locally and therefore queried different attributes. Direct inspection showed the original `#SX` attributes were present. Its missing-attribute conclusions were **test errors**, not provider failures. The harness now serializes exact originating names in `origin.plist`, validates them, and queries those names on the peer. It rejects older manifests without names instead of guessing. The desired `ONLY_SAVING` intent behavior is observational on runtimes that omit the bit, not a failing Apple-contract assertion. Corrected fresh fixtures confirmed: - All five syncable source attributes, including the exact `#SX`/`#PSX` names created on 26, arrived with equal bytes on 14. The reverse run likewise preserved its exact five syncable names. Nonsyncable local-seal attributes did not arrive. - The fresh staged incarnation/revision values arrived and matched the corresponding new bodies. This is converged endpoint evidence, not proof of intermediate body/metadata atomicity. - `#NS` also traveled with sync despite the intent evaluator's never-preserve result. Preserve-for-copy/save intent evaluation is not a universal transport enforcement mechanism.
entries.command: Follow this section's exact commands and scenario matrix; completion evidence is in its linked validation ledger.

entries.name: Validation document: Storage protocol: critical obligations and whole-set audit
entries.purpose: Defines or records Storage protocol: critical obligations and whole-set audit. Consult its status, revision, platform limits, command blocks and independent observations.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 1
entries.purpose: 1 — **Durable means recoverable, with all dependencies and action metadata.** Every acknowledged operation survives ordinary restart with its complete parent/action closure; an installed operation does not depend on a delivered callback. — A creates/edits, then issues a dependent Delete/Restore before earlier callbacks; B receives descendants before ancestors; either or both crash between installation, retained-pin update, application and receipt. No descendant is applied without its transitive ancestry. — DUR-01, START-01, HIST-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 2
entries.purpose: 2 — **Equal complete history yields equal logical meaning.** After finite input and eventual successful exchange/application, computers agree on live births, represented revisions, conflicts, Deletes and action eligibility independently of arrival order or duplicates. — Concurrent edits, multiple covering Deletes, explicit copies and compensations arrive in opposite orders, with stale cache/restart and later descendants. Exact effect/causal provenance, not merely note count, must agree. — HIST-01, DELETE-01, PUB-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 3
entries.purpose: 3 — **Deletion respects intent, concurrency and birth boundaries.** Unexplained file absence is not a remote NV command; an applicable Delete removes its birth while preserving unobserved concurrent edits. Restore has a fresh birth. — One Mac deletes while another edits offline; a later Delete covers the first edit but not its extension; a restored note and a same-named replacement file exist before the old removal callback runs. Neither restoration nor unrelated bytes are erased. — DELETE-01, IMPORT-01, REC-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 4
entries.purpose: 4 — **Every authored action keeps its exact scope and value.** Note operations, before/after references and action metadata describe the same captured mutation; ordinary edits do not consume unrelated conflict heads. Undo/Redo targets actual compensations, not receipt order. — Two Macs undo the same candidate, each authors further work, one restarts, and the user reviews a compensation after remote changes. Complete groups recover together; siblings and unrelated fields survive; no-op compensation is not a completed action. — HIST-01, PUB-01, DUR-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 5
entries.purpose: 5 — **External-file races never become overwrite/removal permission.** A committed note update and a historical receipt are not proof of what occupies a filename now. — Remote segment arrives while an external editor safely replaces/renames the file and local NV has B→C pending; crash between destination install, source accounting and receipt. Preserve external bytes; advance only the actually settled projection; never clear C with B's completion. — DISC-01, AUTH-01, PUB-01, DELETE-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 6
entries.purpose: 6 — **Admission/retry identity is exact, without replaying consent.** One admitted observation is not repeatedly imported after receipt loss, even if its note is later edited/deleted. A changed preparation needs a new operation identity, not necessarily a new unused birth. — Preview changes during reservation; crash before/after operation durability and twice before receipt; deletion arrives during association review/completion; another file competes for the note. No repeated birth, mutation under an old operation ID, silent re-approval or attachment to a deleted birth. — IMPORT-01, REC-01, HIST-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 7
entries.purpose: 7 — **Private metadata and cleanup cannot lose the only retained input.** Payload/reference/receipt/pin ordering protects both possible complete metadata generations after an uncertain replacement. — New preview becomes durable while an older admitted input remains frozen; Local State replacement or cleanup fails; restart returns old or new metadata. Retained bytes and operation/settlement links remain usable; missing/unreadable source is not abandonment. — DUR-01, CLEAN-01, IMPORT-01, CKPT-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 8
entries.purpose: 8 — **Authority is checked at every actual effect.** Root, store, lifecycle, note, relationship and file generations cannot be transplanted by a delayed callback, pathname reuse or serialized receipt. — Repair/copy/save begins on a valid root, which is replaced while work runs; a same-ID repository or new private store appears at the same path. Stop stale effects while preserving healthy local editing and already retained bytes. — AUTH-01, ROOT-01, PUB-01, REPAIR-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 9
entries.purpose: 9 — **Recovery and repair never manufacture completeness.** Cache loss, missing dependencies, partial copies, unsupported input or inaccessible metadata cannot become editable emptiness or a fabricated successful repair. — Fresh/returning Mac sees a partial snapshot plus later objects, loses private state, or has complementary damaged copies. Repair from exact validated available bytes; activate only with required closure/pin/ownership; preserve displaced evidence. — START-01, CKPT-01, REPAIR-01, BACKUP-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 10
entries.purpose: 10 — **Disposition records only what was actually preserved/selected.** NV conflict-copy attention is separate from source Current; Apple member resolution needs exact durable note/file evidence and only its captured applicable scope. — Reciprocal copies on two Macs, later source/copy edits or Delete, new Apple member, lost completion and dismissal. A disposition cannot delete the original, resolve a later revision or recreate a deliberately deleted copy. — REC-01, HIST-01, WAIT-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 11
entries.purpose: 11 — **Local safety and progress do not depend on provider progress.** Healthy admitted work can become durable offline; waits are bounded/dismissible and never become evidence of absence/newness. — Provider withholds an object indefinitely while local edits, close/cancel and independent pending items continue. Only actual local durability/ownership/key failures close admission; no fair user approval or unconditional network delivery is assumed. — DUR-01, ROOT-01, WAIT-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: Most critical properties / 12
entries.purpose: 12 — **Storage trust and copy boundaries remain honest.** Authentication, immutable naming, profile/key separation and ownership must precede decoding/use; a repository copy preserves available history but cannot claim undisclosed or unpublished data. — Duplicated/reordered/corrupt envelopes, restored writer state, credential cutover failure, foreign same-named object and provider-only reconstruction. Never reuse nonce/identity for different bytes, downgrade encryption or erase the only usable source/key. — CRYPT-01, BACKUP-01, AUTH-01
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.id: planned-check:docs/tla/Storage-Protocol-Audit.md#What remains insufficiently modeled / Object/action/dependency/pin durability on both hosts
entries.name: What remains insufficiently modeled / Object/action/dependency/pin durability on both hosts
entries.purpose: Object/action/dependency/pin durability on both hosts — Installer, deletion, action and repair components — Carry the same payload/action group through file/name/directory barriers, transitive closure, pin replacement, acceptance, both crashes and replay. Several current `Install` actions still abstract the complete barrier; one passing installer plus one passing receiver is not a composition proof.

entries.name: What remains insufficiently modeled / Pending-file ownership through import/association and repeated recovery
entries.purpose: Pending-file ownership through import/association and repeated recovery — Reference/lifecycle/association components plus `ExternalRecoveryBridge` — The added bridge carries A/B ownership, pin/reference/settlement races, installed-before-ack work, peer Delete and two recovery cuts. Remaining: settings/credential replacements, competing file claims and arbitrary value/codec/closure integration in that same bridge. It inlines a bounded protocol, not a refinement of the complete installers.

entries.name: What remains insufficiently modeled / Projection A→B while C and external replacement race
entries.purpose: Projection A→B while C and external replacement race — Transition/catalog/stamp/deletion components plus `ProjectionRecoveryBridge` — The added bridge carries exact output tokens, compare-after-replace/displaced backup ownership, source accounting, receipts, peer history, delayed Delete, restored occupant and restart. Remaining: full causal Delete/conflict retraction, actual association/provenance classification, physical filesystems and arbitrary save failures.

entries.purpose: Compensation encountering same-birth remote alternatives during installation — Shared causal reducer and `CompensationOverlapBridge`, plus native/action components — The added bridge checks actual before/after values, same-note overlap/disjoint/competing/observing inputs, unchosen heads, later inverse, local Current-pin release and cross-host/restart convergence. Remaining: native remaining-effect attribution, partial/multi-family groups, text and real installer/UI integration.
entries.command: Use the commands/implementation witnesses named in this section. A matrix row is a specified check; qualification is established only by its linked result ledger.

entries.name: What remains insufficiently modeled / Apple setter, verification query and independent observers
entries.purpose: Apple setter, verification query and independent observers — Two scoped-disposition components plus API contract probes — Real installed-file/root generations, segment/pin barrier, crash/reopen, setter failure, later successful query and independently delayed provider disclosures must connect. The component's shared resolved set is an abstraction, not immediate cross-Mac propagation or proof of badge settlement.

entries.name: What remains insufficiently modeled / Repair/transition/quit under real namespace and key failures
entries.purpose: Repair/transition/quit under real namespace and key failures — Repair/bootstrap/local-lane/copy checks — Destination-name race winners, foreign/wrong-kind replacements, private-store loss during provider reconstruction, pin-commit crash, private pending payload preservation, single-owner draining and source-preserving encrypted cutover remain uncomposed. The three added repair races are separate scenarios, not every simultaneous root/store failure. No TLA model proves cryptography, `fsync`, APFS power-loss behavior or provider availability.

arguments: --skip-build; action='store_true'; help='Use already refreshed app objects'
--sqlcipher-build; help='Isolated source build containing sqlite3.h and libsqlite3.a'
--zstd-prefix; help='Optional experiment-only prefix containing include/zstd.h and lib/libzstd.a'
--zstd-min-match; choices=[0, 4, 6]; default=0; help="0 uses the selected level's default"
--dictionary-size; choices=[0, 8192, 32768, 65536]; default=0; help='Train a private shared dictionary when recompressing current cells'
--dictionary-pattern; choices=['words', 'mixed', 'random']; default='words'; help='Independent synthetic training family; may differ from measured notes'

--dictionary-training; choices=['held-out', 'current', 'all-current']; default='held-out'; help='Independent generated records, a bounded current-cell sample, or every current cell (128-MiB fixture limit)'
--dictionary-sample-limit; default=1024; help='Maximum current cells considered for sampled training'
--dictionary-sample-budget; default=8 * 1024 * 1024; help='Maximum total decoded bytes retained for sampled training'
--dictionary-contracts; action='store_true'; help='Small-fixture dictionary faults and abrupt-exit transaction checks'
--expect-training-fallback; action='store_true'; help='Negative control: require training to decline and complete startup without dictionary cells'
--dictionary-micro-baseline; help='Additional alternating decode-only comparison with a matching no-dictionary store.sqlite'
--dictionary-example-comparison; action='store_true'; help='Compare strict wrapper, official-example core API, and refDDict API on validated frames'
--aged; action='store_true'; help='Actual-DDL, clean-exit locality experiment; ignores --kinds'
--context-bytes; default=256; help='Synthetic authoring-reference bytes per current cell'
--secondary; action='store_true'; help='Also vary page-cache size, temporary lifetimes and raw reads'
--reuse-aged-root; help='Reuse completed clean fixture images; write new measurements separately'
--source-layout; choices=LAYOUTS; help='Use this layout from --reuse-aged-root as the immutable source for NEW variants'
--rewrite-passes; default=1; help='Repeat the chosen physical layout operation without intervening logical changes'
--rewrite-cache-kib; default=0; help='0 preserves the existing maintenance connection default'
--rewrite-secure-delete; choices=['default', 'off']; default='default'; help='Synthetic cost-isolation control only; not a privacy policy change'
--rewrite-chunk-mib; default=0; help='Native SQLite VFS chunk-size hint; not a B-tree reservation'
--reserve-budget-mib; default=16; help='Maximum temporary payload in bounded-reserved control'
--read-ahead; choices=['default', 'off']; default='default'; help="Aged probe's measured read descriptor only"
--hole-interval; default=0; help='Retain then release a 16-KiB private buffer every N mutations (0=off)'
--cell-codec; choices=['raw', 'zlib', 'zstd']; default='raw'; help='Aged experiment only: independently compressed current cells'
--cell-decoder; choices=['allocate', 'scratch', 'stream']; default='allocate'; help='Per-cell allocation baseline, reusable output buffer, or buffer plus reusable inflater'
--body-pattern; choices=['words', 'random', 'mixed']; default='words'; help='Aged experiment: repeated words, high-entropy ASCII, or six mixed note genres'
--prefetch-workers; choices=[1, 4, 8, 16]; default=1; help='Bounded raw ciphertext read-ahead concurrency'
--prefetch-amplification; choices=[1, 2, 4]; default=1; help='Coalesce ranges with at most this ratio of read pages to requested current pages'
--hint-fault; choices=['none', 'empty', 'malformed', 'wrong-pages']; default='none'; help='Read-ahead hint fault injection; all note values must still come from ordinary SQL'
